sentiment.instructions: Judge the overall sentiment the tweet's author expresses (about events, people, plans, products), not just the topic. Tweets are SemEval-style, often mentioning dates, celebrities, sports or politics; decide what feeling the author conveys.

criteria.positive: Author shows excitement, enjoyment, praise, hope or anticipation: plans or events framed eagerly (going to a show, game, party tomorrow), congratulations, good luck wishes, fandom praise, promotions urging people to watch/attend. Cues: 'Happy Sunday', 'can't wait', 'excited', 'Go Colts!!', 'best', 'love', 'bless', 'Woot', 'Who's going?!', ':)', 'good luck', 'Praise God', 'I want'. Light sarcasm or teasing still counts as positive if the tone is upbeat; praise even of controversial things counts.
criteria.neutral: Factual reports, news headlines, scores, schedules, job ads, customer-service replies, plain questions or invitations without expressed emotion ('Who going with me to...?'), and mixed or mild opinions/jokes without clear feeling. Also mild snark or speculative remarks that aren't clearly angry or sad ('makes me not want to go', 'may not be in love with him anymore'). When unsure between neutral and a polar label with weak cues, choose neutral.
criteria.negative: Author expresses anger, disappointment, sadness, frustration, insult, contempt or hostility: complaints about delays, missed events, bad performances, political/religious attacks, wishing harm, grief, exhaustion. Cues: 'WTF', 'FML', 'damn', 'sucks', 'idiot', 'pissed', 'worst', 'joke', 'crying', 'grieving', 'tragedy', 'cringeworthy', profanity aimed at someone, sarcastic insults.
